record.context_brief: Lozenge tilings of a three-hole semiregular hexagon
record.original_question: Find an exact enumeration formula for lozenge tilings of the hexagon with side lengths 2n, 2n+3, 2n, 2n+3, 2n, 2n+3 after removing the triangle centered on each of the three long sides.

evidence.quote: One can also look take a 2n, 2n + 3, 2n, 2n + 3, 2n, 2n + 3 hexagon and make it lozenge-tilable by removing a triangle from the middle of each of its three long sides, as shown below:
Problem 3: Enumerate the lozenge-tilings of the region obtained from the 2n, 2n+ 3, 2n, 2n+ 3, 2n, 2n+ 3 hexagon by removing a triangle from the middle of each of its long sides.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider, on the triangular lattice, a semiregular hexagon with side lengths (2n, 2n+3, 2n, 2n+3, 2n, 2n+3) taken in cyclic order, where n is a positive integer. The three sides of length 2n+3 are the "long sides". From the middle of each long side, remove the unique unit triangle that is centered on that side and points into the hexagon (i.e., for each long side, delete the central up- or down-pointing unit triangle whose base lies on that side). Let R_n denote the resulting region. A lozenge tiling of R_n is a covering of R_n by unit rhombi (lozenges), each formed by two unit triangles sharing an edge, with no overlap.

Find a closed-form (product) formula for the number of lozenge tilings of R_n as a function of n. More generally, give a q-analog enumerating these tilings weighted by an appropriate q-statistic.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (Propp's Problem 3) was solved by Tri Lai in "A q-enumeration of lozenge tilings of a hexagon with three dents," Advances in Applied Mathematics 82 (2017), 23–57, which provides an explicit product (q-)enumeration formula. Subsequent works (Ciucu–Lai–Rohatgi, and others) have further generalized this result.

status_evidence.title: A q-enumeration of lozenge tilings of a hexagon with three dents
status_evidence.snippet: The unweighted version of the result generalizes a problem posed by James Propp on enumeration of lozenge tilings of a hexagon of side-lengths 2n, 2n+3, 2n, 2n+3, 2n, 2n+3 with the central unit triangles on the (2n+3)-sides removed.
status_evidence.claim: Tri Lai's 2017 paper provides an exact q-enumeration formula, solving Propp's Problem 3.

status_evidence.title: Problems in the enumeration of tilings — Tri Lai
status_evidence.snippet: Lai's formula for hexagons with three dents... follows as immediate special case.
status_evidence.claim: Lai's three-dents formula is established and used as a known result.
